title: Runtime parameter sanitization and human-friendly error mapping
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Problem: Tool/function calls surface a mixture of machine-centric JSON Schema validation errors and model inference errors that are hard for application developers to consume. Current validator behavior often returns raw schema paths and technical messages (e.g., "/params/body must be integer") without suggestions or recovery actions. We need a runtime layer that sanitizes inputs, applies safe coercions where appropriate, and maps low-level failures to concise, actionable, human-friendly error objects that driving applications and SDKs can display or act upon. Goals: reduce customer friction when authoring tool calls, enable graceful runtime fallback (coercion or defaulting) while preserving strict opt-in validation for security-sensitive params, improve telemetry to make common authoring mistakes discoverable, and provide consistent error codes for programmatic handling.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime accepts extended JSON Schema annotations (see design_notes) and uses them when present
Validator will attempt safe coercions for configured fields and only fail when coercion is not possible or disabled
Errors exposed to API/SDK consumers follow the agreed error contract: code, human_message, field_path, attempted_value, suggestion (optional)
A/B rollout: 10% of hosted runtime traffic uses smart sanitizer with detailed telemetry; toggle controlled by customer config for Dedicated/Private
End-to-end tests cover coercion paths, explicit validation failures, and error mapping for at least 8 representative tool schemas
design_notes: High-level approach: introduce lightweight JSON Schema extensions that are purely advisory at runtime. Example extensions: "x-coerce": ["number_from_string", "trim"], "x-normalizer": "lowercase", "x-strict": true (opt-in to disallow coercion), and "x-suggest": "use ISO-8601 date". Validator will run three ordered stages: 1) normalization (string trims, unicode NFC), 2) coercion (string->number, string->boolean, csv->array) when x-coerce permits, 3) strict schema validation. On failure, construct error objects mapped to a small set of stable error codes (e.g., INVALID_TYPE, COERCION_FAILED, MISSING_REQUIRED, EXTERNAL_REF_FAILURE). Each code maps to a short human_message and an optional suggestion. Provide an SDK-side error wrapper that surfaces both machine-friendly fields and localized human messages. For compatibility, fall back to existing validator behavior when no extensions are present.
implementation_plan: Define JSON Schema extension names and canonical semantics in a short spec doc (contributor: @priyak)
Implement x-normalizer and x-coerce handlers in the runtime validation library as pure functions with unit tests
Add an error-mapping layer that translates internal validator exceptions to the public error contract and stable error codes
Instrument telemetry: metric for coercion_count, coercion_failure_count, validation_failure_by_field, and a slow-path counter for schemas with refs
Add customer toggle in config: validation.mode = [strict|coerce|off] with default = coerce for hosted
Integrate with SDKs: expose both raw error payload and formatted human_message; update JS/Go SDKs to render suggestion field in debug mode
Rollout: feature-flag to 10% traffic, collect telemetry for 2 weeks, review, then ramp or revert
testing_plan: Unit test matrix for normalization and coercion rules with edge cases (unicode, leading/trailing whitespace, large ints)
Property-based tests to ensure coercion is idempotent when x-strict is false
Integration tests: mock tool schema with nested objects and arrays to validate field_path reporting
E2E smoke on hosted cluster with sample tool (reranker) and multiple client SDKs to assert error contract
User acceptance test: have PM and DX review 10 sample messages for clarity and actionable suggestions
